lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- José Eduardo Alves | Lesson 7 -- Comparing Deals, Programs and Cities

listenings.text: People ask me which program is the best, and that is the wrong question. The right question is: the best for what? Take the two on your list. The first one is older, it is more famous, and its admission rate is the lowest in the country, which means the competition is brutal. The second one is younger and less famous, but the classes are smaller, the professors answer their email, and the campus is twenty minutes from the port authority. If you want a name on a wall, the first one is better. If you want people who work on the same problems as you, the second one is better, and it is not close. And one more thing that nobody puts in a ranking. The most important number for a person who is fifty and still working is not the ranking. It is how flexible the timetable is.

Every year somebody asks me whether Santos or Paranagua is the better port, and my answer never changes. Santos is bigger, it is faster on paper, and it moves more cargo than any other port in South America. Paranagua is smaller and the queue is usually longer, but it is closer to the farms in the south, so the trucks are cheaper and they arrive sooner. Now here is the part that matters for a lawyer. The most expensive difference between the two is not the freight. It is the contract. A shorter route with a more complex clause can cost you more than a longer route with a simple one, because the complex clause is the one somebody argues about in January. The cheapest deal on the page is very often the most expensive deal of the year.
